new_entities.name: Clozapine for treatment-resistant schizophrenia
new_entities.description: Use of clozapine as maintenance antipsychotic treatment in patients with schizophrenia who have not responded adequately to other agents.

new_entities.name: Relapse prevention
new_entities.description: Lower risk of relapse, rehospitalization, or clinical deterioration during maintenance treatment.

edges.population: adults with schizophrenia or related psychotic disorders, especially treatment-resistant or high-relapse populations
edges.mechanism: Clozapine likely lowers relapse partly by providing broader receptor coverage and better symptom control in refractory illness, while also reducing hostility and severe behavioral destabilization that often drive rehospitalization. Its maintenance advantage may also reflect better efficacy in people who have already failed standard antipsychotics.
edges.summary: The maintenance signal for clozapine is real, but it comes more from comparative meta-analysis and large real-world effectiveness data than from neat placebo-style relapse trials. Across longer-term schizophrenia evidence, clozapine repeatedly sits near the top for keeping difficult-to-treat patients out of relapse or discontinuation.
edges.caveats: This is not a clean first-line edge: clozapine is usually reserved for treatment-resistant disease and brings substantial monitoring burdens. Some of its apparent relapse-prevention advantage may also reflect channeling into specialist care and differences in adherence monitoring.

evidence.notes: Efficacy and effectiveness of antipsychotics in schizophrenia: network meta-analyses combining evidence from randomised controlled trials and real-world data.
Long-term effectiveness of oral second-generation antipsychotics in patients with schizophrenia and related disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis of direct head-to-head comparisons.

evidence.citation: GlickID et al 2011 J Clin Psychiatry
